data.answer: This query totals the number of lines in non-test files for each package. It reads the file inventory, keeps only files that are not marked as tests and that belong to an actual package (top-level modules with no package are left out), sums each file's line count per package, and then ranks packages from the largest total to the smallest, breaking ties alphabetically by package name and returning only the top five.

display_annotations.note: Deterministic display links; not source citations made by the model.

output_contract.guidance: Return each package and its total line count. Order by lines descending, then package ascending.

data.question: Which packages under auto_ontology have the most lines of non-test code? Give the top five.
data.reference_sql:
SELECT package, SUM(line_count) AS lines
FROM code.files
WHERE package LIKE 'auto_ontology%' AND NOT is_test
GROUP BY package
ORDER BY lines DESC, package
LIMIT 5;

request.question:
Which packages under auto_ontology have the most lines of non-test code? Give the top five.

Requested output columns: package (string), lines (integer).
Return every requested field using exactly its specified column alias. Preserve complete case-sensitive repository-relative paths and symbol IDs; do not substitute display names. Include all requested counts and provenance fields. Explain the query result in ordinary prose; do not emit placeholder text. These questions concern a static map of open-source Python code. Describe what the query computes and the assumptions it makes; the returned rows are reported separately. Questions asking which files, modules or symbols mean distinct identities, not one repeated row per matching import or call occurrence; preserve occurrence counts only when requested. Caller/callee graph questions include methods as well as standalone functions unless a symbol kind is explicitly restricted. Use files.is_test for test-file classification; test_links describe associations, not the complete set of test files. Use DOUBLE or DECIMAL, rather than single-precision REAL, for percentage calculations.
Return each package and its total line count. Order by lines descending, then package ascending.

data.sql: SELECT package AS package, SUM(line_count) AS lines FROM auto_ontology_code.code.files WHERE is_test = false AND package <> '' GROUP BY package ORDER BY lines DESC, package ASC LIMIT 5
